origin_scene.summary: Diagnosing why a generated cockscomb barite had plausible ingredients but the wrong aggregate topology.

carries.text: Repeated squat, broad tablets share a dominant stacking axis.
Tablets overlap face-to-face and step or fan laterally.
Partly exposed rims create a tower or comb-like silhouette.
Individual tablets remain legible within a coherent aggregate.

does_not_carry.text: Calcite chemistry, cleavage, terminations, transparency, color, and luster do not transfer to barite.
Poker chip does not require geometrically perfect discs or uniform spacing.
A radial multi-axis rosette is not a tower merely because its individuals are coin-like.
The mapping does not specify matrix, staining, damage, or later mineral overgrowth.

parity.text: One dominant stacking axis remains readable.
Repeated broad tablets overlap primarily face-to-face.
The aggregate silhouette emerges from stepped exposed rims, not elongated fins.

extensions.novel_case: A cockscomb barite modeled as upright glass fins
extensions.consequence: Shorten and widen individuals, increase face overlap, preserve lateral stepping, and avoid upright fins.

break_ledger.proposed_break: A barite or azurite rose also contains coin-like tablets.
break_ledger.reason: The rose radiates and interpenetrates across multiple orientations; it violates the dominant shared stacking axis and is a negative case.

conduct_events.decision_context: Choose the next procedural aggregate instruction.
conduct_events.counterfactual: Retain radial or upright coin-like tablets.
conduct_events.observed_change: Specified squat broad tablets, face overlap, one stacking axis, lateral steps, and readable rims.
